newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli stocks led by bank shares close up.
newsitem.headline: Israeli stocks led by bank shares close up.

text.p: Tel Aviv shares closed higher on Tuesday led by a rise in the banking sector, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.11 percent, or 2.15 points, to 195.23 on a low all-share turnover of 60 million shekels against 40 million on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index gained 2.37 percent to 204.74.
"The whole banking sector rose today on hopes for the improved results," said Shar Gazit at Batucha Securities and investments.

The First International Bank of Israel gained 0.25 percent to 34,763 after it reported third-quarter net profit of 54.2 million shekels against 33.3 million shekels a year earlier. Traders said the bank's share did not rise more because the report was published just before the end of the trading day.
"The good report published by the First International Bank was a very good sign. This was the first report released by one of the big banks," Gazit added.
A trader at Bank Hapoalim noted that volume continues to be low and Tuesday's gains, following two days of declines, therefore were not significant.
"Share prices are very cheap now and investors are looking for a trigger that will spark the market," he said.
Elbit surged 4.0 percent to 14,024. Traders attributed the rise to a technical correction.

The most active shares were Bank Hapoalim, which gained 2.25 percent to 461 on volume of 4.7 million shekels; Koor Industries, which rose 0.75 percent to 28,810 on turnover of 2.2 million shekels; and Bank Leumi, which gained 1.75 percent to 387 on volume of 2.2 million shekels.
